summary: I re-verified every claim in the prior audit against source. The core structural picture holds: app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx is a real, reachable, timeout-guarded composition (10 parallel arms with withTimeoutFallback, lines 267-313), the by-key route permanent-redirects into it, JSON-LD (breadcrumb + realEstateListing) ships, and the mobile flow is genuine. Their field-count claim was exact (DETAIL_SELECT is precisely 87 entries; `details` is read exactly once for StreetSuffix; `amenities` jsonb is never read at all). Their CTA-context finding, their filler-stub finding, and their dead-SimilarListings finding all reproduce verbatim. Two corrections: (a) the media-suppression leak is WORSE than reported — there are two independent bypass paths, not one (listing_tile_mv has no media_suppressed projection, AND the OG route's fallback getHeroPhotosByListingKeys at lib/data/listings/getListingDetailBundles.ts:65-82 queries listing_photos with zero suppression check; similar_listings_mv also carries a bare photo_url); (b) their "missing" verdict on dual-sided conversion is wrong — they grepped only app/listing and components/site/listing-detail and missed the KbFooter that the page actually renders, which carries a live /sell/valuation "What's my home worth" link, and a complete saved-search + alert-cron system exists site-wide. I also found a conversion-path failure they missed entirely: the entire sticky broker card AND mobile contact bar are gated on ctaBroker, which is null whenever getBrokers() hits its 3s timeout fallback — a slow pooler silently removes every contact CTA from the page.

items.requirement: Expose and leverage the ~800 fields per MLS record
items.evidence: lib/data/listings/getListingDetail.ts lines 35-131: DETAIL_SELECT is exactly 87 entries (counted programmatically, not estimated). The raw `details` jsonb is referenced exactly once, line 51 ('StreetSuffix:details->>StreetSuffix'); grep for 'details' in that file returns only that line plus the unrelated typed column `foundation_details` (lines 102, 197, 344). The `amenities` jsonb column (docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md line 96) is read NOWHERE in the detail path. supabase/migrations/20260711160000_listing_search_mv.sql lines 37-47 define public.rr_feature_keys(), applied at lines 131-166 to flatten KitchenAppliances, Flooring, Heating, etc. Consumers of listing_search_mv, verified by grep across lib/ and app/: lib/data/listings/searchListingsAll.ts:655,726, lib/data/admin/remarksSearch.ts:98, and the search actions in app/actions/listings.ts / app/actions/search.ts. Zero listing-detail consumers.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Reproduced exactly, including the 87-column figure. Adding: the auditor undersold it — the `amenities` jsonb is a second entirely-unread structured source, not just `details`. The rr_feature_keys() extraction is one join away from the detail page and is used only to power filter checkboxes the buyer already ticked before arriving.
items.why_it_matters: The one page a buyer lands on from an ad shows less structured detail than the search filters that got them there. Shop/outbuilding, RV parking, owner-carry, well/septic and STR-allowed are the exact Central Oregon differentiators, already extracted, invisible.

items.requirement: Owner media-suppression flag respected everywhere a listing's photo can appear
items.evidence: Enforcement confirmed on the detail page's own reads: lib/data/listings/getListingPhotos.ts:91 (`if (detail?.media_suppressed === true) return []`), lib/data/videos/getListingVideos.ts:160-181, lib/data/listings/getListingDetail.ts:282 (`photoUrl: row.media_suppressed ? null : row.PhotoURL`). Leak path 1: supabase/migrations/20260708150000_listing_tile_mv_street_suffix.sql line 52 (`l."PhotoURL" AS photo_url`) — grep for media_suppressed across every listing_tile_mv migration returns nothing, and lib/data/listings/getListingTiles.ts applies no such filter. Leak path 2 (MISSED by the prior audit): app/api/og/route.tsx lines 34-38 falls back to getHeroPhotosByListingKeys when tile.photoUrl is empty; that function, lib/data/listings/getListingDetailBundles.ts:65-82, selects listing_key/photo_url from `listing_photos` with only `.eq('is_hero', true)` — no suppression check whatsoever. Leak path 3: the same migration line 115-117 defines similar_listings_mv selecting a bare photo_url. Leak path 4: listing_search_mv (20260711160000) line 79 also projects `l."PhotoURL" AS photo_url` with no suppression in its WHERE (line 169), so suppressed listings surface in search results. Blast radius on the detail page itself: lib/kb/fetch-nearby-tiles.ts:41-56 calls getListingTiles for the 'similar homes' rail rendered at page.tsx:588.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor found one bypass; there are four, and they missed the most direct one — getHeroPhotosByListingKeys reads listing_photos raw with no flag check at all, which is the OG route's own fallback path.] An owner's explicit photo-removal request is honored on exactly one surface and bypassed on the share-preview image, the search results grid, the similar-listings rail, and the bulk hero-photo helper. This is a broker-liability item, not a polish item.
items.why_it_matters: Matt is the licensed principal broker. An owner who formally requested photo removal can still see their home's photo in a shared link preview and in site search.

items.requirement: CTAs must be thoroughly thought through
items.evidence: components/site/listing-detail/ClimateRiskBlock.tsx line 148: href="/contact?intent=climate-report" — confirmed, no listingKey. components/site/listing-detail/VacationRentalPotential.tsx line 89: href="/contact?intent=vacation-rental-projection" — confirmed, no listingKey. app/contact/page.tsx: `const intent = params.intent === 'tour' ? 'tour' : params.intent === 'question' ? 'question' : undefined` — a two-value whitelist; both strings above fall through to undefined. The listing-context tile on the same page is gated on `params.listingKey ? await getListingTiles(...) : null`, so it renders nothing for these two links. Contrast the CTAs that DO carry context: components/site/listing-detail/ListingMobileContactBar.client.tsx line 40 and components/site/kb/KbFooter.client.tsx lines 63-68, both of which build `/contact?listingKey=...&intent=tour`.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Exact, line-for-line. Worth stating more bluntly than the auditor did: the codebase already has the correct pattern in three other places on the same page, so this is inconsistency, not an unbuilt feature.
items.why_it_matters: The two most differentiated CTAs on the page dump the visitor on a blank generic form with no record of what they asked for.

items.requirement: Every page conveys we are the experts with all the information (no filler)
items.evidence: app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx lines 451-453: `<ClimateRiskBlock risk={null} /> <VacationRentalPotential projection={null} /> <TransparentCMASummary cma={null} />`, under a comment claiming 'No fake numbers'. components/site/listing-detail/ClimateRiskBlock.tsx lines 128-155: the null branch renders a fixed paragraph naming FEMA/Deschutes County WUI/NOAA sources it does not actually query, ending 'Detailed scoring for this property is on request' — identical on every listing in the portfolio. components/site/listing-detail/TransparentCMASummary.tsx:39 `if (cma == null) return null` — that import and JSX line are pure dead weight; the section can never render. components/site/listing-detail/SimilarListings.tsx: repo-wide grep across app/, components/, lib/ finds only its own definition at line 39 — zero importers. Confirmed dead. (Note: components/listing/SimilarListings.tsx and components/listing/ListingSimilarListings.tsx are separate, distinct files; the dead one is the site/listing-detail copy.)
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Reproduced. Sharper framing than the auditor gave: naming FEMA, the Deschutes County WUI map and NOAA in copy while querying none of them is closer to a §0 violation than a stub — it implies sourcing that does not exist behind it.
items.why_it_matters: Identical boilerplate on every listing is the exact opposite of expert positioning, and the sourcing language overstates what the page actually knows.

items.requirement: Ultimate goal: convert to buyer AND seller clients
items.evidence: REFUTING the prior 'missing' verdict. app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx line 590 renders `<KbFooter towns={[]} listingKey={listing.listingKey} />`. components/site/kb/KbFooter.client.tsx lines 133-136 render a persistent 'Sellers' nav column with `<Link href="/sell/valuation">What's my home worth</Link>` and `<Link href="/sell">Sell your home</Link>` — unconditional, present on every listing page. What IS true: lines 22-24 and 61-70 show the prominent CTA band deliberately swaps the seller pair for tour/ask-about-this-home whenever listingKey is passed, with an explicit design-audit P2 comment justifying it. Separately, a full saved-search system exists and is reachable: app/actions/saved-searches.ts, app/actions/saved-search-alerts.ts, app/api/cron/saved-search-alerts/route.ts, app/account/saved-searches/page.tsx, app/dashboard/searches/page.tsx. It is simply never surfaced on the listing detail page. The listing page's own conversion set is PriceCtaStrip (tour/ask/save/share, verified in components/site/listing-detail/PriceCtaStrip.tsx) plus ListingBrokerCTA.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor graded this 'missing' on a grep scoped to app/listing and components/site/listing-detail only. That scope excludes KbFooter, which the page renders and which carries a live /sell/valuation link. They also asserted zero 'saved search' hits repo-wide, which is flatly false — there is a saved-search table, server actions, an alert cron and two account surfaces.] The real gap is narrower and more defensible: the seller hook is demoted to footer nav (an intentional decision, commented), and the saved-search prompt — the single highest-value buyer-capture ask on an ad-landing page — is never offered here despite the machinery being built and running.
items.why_it_matters: The infrastructure for both sides already ships. This is a surfacing decision, not a build, which makes the effort estimate much lower than the prior report implied.

items.requirement: Flow logically end to end, mobile-first
items.evidence: Section order confirmed at app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx lines 391-455 exactly as reported. components/site/listing-detail/ListingDetailShell.tsx lines 142-153: single mobile column, `lg:grid-cols-[1.6fr_360px]` only at lg. components/site/PhotoGalleryLightbox.tsx lines 75, 80, 146-147: real onTouchStart/onTouchEnd swipe. Timeout guards real — page.tsx lines 267-313, ten withTimeoutFallback arms. BUT: page.tsx line 457 `const sidebar = ctaBroker ? (...) : null`, and line 344 `const ctaBroker = listingAgent ?? matt`, where `matt` (lines 338-343) resolves from `brokers`, which comes from `withTimeoutFallback(getBrokers(), [], 3000, 'listing:brokers')` at line 281. An empty array makes every fallback arm null, so ctaBroker is null, so the sidebar is null. components/site/listing-detail/ListingBrokerCTA.client.tsx line 116 renders ListingMobileContactBar from INSIDE that same component (page.tsx line 76 explicitly voids the import). Therefore a single 3-second broker-query timeout removes the desktop contact card AND the mobile sticky bar simultaneously — the page degrades to zero broker contact affordance with no fallback.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor graded this 'have' and treated the sticky mobile bar as the reliable safety net for the bottom-of-DOM contact card. It is not a net — it lives inside the very component that disappears. Both contact paths share one failure point, and that failure point is a timeout arm the auditor itself cited as evidence of robustness.] The ordering and responsiveness are genuinely good; the reachability is conditional in a way that fails silently and unobservably on exactly the slow-database conditions the timeout guards were added for.
items.why_it_matters: Under pooler stall the #1 ad-landing page still renders 200 OK, looks fine, and has no way to contact anyone. Nothing logs or alarms on it.

items.requirement: OG / share image present for a listing
items.evidence: app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx line 172: ogImage: `/api/og?type=listing&id=...`. app/api/og/route.tsx exists, `export const runtime = 'edge'` (line 13), renders 1200x630 at lines 44-80 — route is real and reachable. Confirmed off-brand: line 69, `backgroundColor: '#d4a853'` on the price badge, against a Design System v2 palette locked to navy #102742 / cream #faf8f4 with gold explicitly retired (CLAUDE.md, 2026-05-12/13). I could not find a design-token gate script covering app/api (scripts/check-design-tokens.mjs does not exist at that path), so nothing mechanically catches this. Suppression leak confirmed twice over on this exact route: tile.photoUrl from the unfiltered listing_tile_mv, and the getHeroPhotosByListingKeys fallback at lines 34-38 which reads listing_photos with no flag check.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor graded this 'have' and filed the defects as an afterthought in the gap field. An OG image that renders a retired brand color and can publish a photo the owner formally asked to be removed is not a completed capability — it ships a compliance exposure on the single most-shared asset the site produces.] Downgraded to partial on both counts.
items.why_it_matters: This image is the click-through driver for every shared listing link and the one surface where a suppression leak is most public.

items.requirement: (supporting) Verify that fields the detail page already selects actually have data upstream
items.evidence: Render branches confirmed present: components/site/listing-detail/PropertySpecs.tsx line 164 (propertyAttachedYn), 171-172 (storiesTotal), 176-177 (fireplacesTotal), 261-262 (walkScore). Corresponding DETAIL_SELECT entries confirmed: 'stories_total', 'fireplaces_total', 'property_attached_yn', 'spa_yn', 'walk_score'. items.gap: [VERIFIED] Their honesty here was correct and I could not improve on it. Flagging one thing they should have said: this is the single item in the report whose resolution changes the priority of item 1, and it is answerable in one query by anyone with DB access. It should be closed before anyone estimates the rich-feature work.
items.why_it_matters: If these promoted columns are structurally null for on-market listings, the detail page's apparent field coverage is inflated and the unused rr_feature_keys() data becomes the only real path to depth.

shared_primitives_needed: media_suppressed projected into listing_tile_mv, listing_search_mv and similar_listings_mv, AND a suppression filter added to getHeroPhotosByListingKeys (lib/data/listings/getListingDetailBundles.ts:65) — four call sites, not one. A CI gate asserting no photo-returning DAL function ships without a media_suppressed check would prevent the fifth.
A reusable rich-RETS read path exposing rr_feature_keys() output (and the unread `amenities` jsonb) to the listing-detail DAL, so detail page, CMA, flyers and carousels share one extraction.

A shared /contact intent enum validated at both ends, so a CTA cannot invent an intent string that silently degrades to a contextless form (app/contact/page.tsx currently hardcodes a two-value whitelist).

A non-null fallback contract for the broker CTA: ctaBroker must resolve to a hardcoded principal-broker constant when getBrokers() times out, so the page can never render with zero contact affordance. Plus an alarm on withTimeoutFallback firing on the 'listing:brokers' arm.
A design-token gate that covers app/api/**/*.tsx — the OG route's retired-gold hex proves the current gate chain does not reach image-generation routes.
open_questions_for_owner: Climate risk and vacation rental currently name FEMA, the Deschutes County WUI map and NOAA in copy while querying none of them. Hide those sections until real data is wired, or keep the 'on request' CTA and strip the source names so the page does not imply sourcing it does not have?

The seller CTA is intentionally demoted to footer nav on listing pages (commented as design-audit P2 — a buyer who just read a listing should not get a 'what's your home worth' pitch). Do you want that decision kept, or should the listing page carry a seller hook above the footer?
The saved-search + alert system is fully built and running but never offered on the listing detail page. Add a 'get alerts for homes like this' prompt there, and if so, at what scroll depth?

Of the 36 rich RETS feature categories already extracted for search (shop/outbuilding, RV parking, owner-carry terms, septic/well, STR-allowed HOA rules, irrigation source, appliances, flooring), which should surface on the public listing page first?
Should a suppressed-media listing be excluded from the similar-listings rail and search results entirely, or appear with a placeholder image? The fix differs materially between those two answers.
